walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: The coordinator is a separate thread with its own model and settings, and the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse, which goes on working while it talks.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked
beats.body: What the coordinator may ask for is a manifest pinned by digest, and every call is validated against it before it runs. A call that has already run is not run again.

beats.heading: Archboard brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. Archboard passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While a recording holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. Pane news goes to the voice model alone, and only for what the user changed by hand.

beats.heading: An approval is answered once
beats.body: A final spoken reply arms a gate on one approval. Whether it is then answered out loud or in the pane, it settles exactly once, and an unproven answer falls back to the narrowest outcome.

walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a separate thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorse and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse, which goes on working while it talks. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked
beats.body: What the coordinator may ask for is a manifest pinned by digest, and every call is validated against it before it runs. A call that has already run is not run again.

beats.heading: Archboard brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. Archboard passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While a recording holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. Pane news goes to the voice model alone, and only for what the user changed by hand.

beats.heading: An approval is answered once
beats.body: A final spoken reply arms a gate on one approval. Whether it is then answered out loud or in the pane, it settles exactly once, and an unproven answer falls back to the narrowest outcome.

beats.heading: Each tab hears only its own threads
beats.body: A tool call or notification goes to the tab session that owns its thread. So a coordinator's tool call runs against its own tab's workhorse, and a workhorse's news reaches only its own tab's coordinator. walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a separate thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It works in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so it names a checkout with -C on every command. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, which goes on working while it talks. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked

beats.heading: Archboard brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. Archboard passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news that names the checkout of the workhorse. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While a recording holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. beats.heading: An approval is answered once

beats.heading: Each tab hears only its own threads

walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a separate thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It works in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so it names a checkout with -C on every command. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, which goes on working while it talks. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked
beats.body: What the coordinator may ask for is a manifest pinned by digest, and every call is validated against it before it runs. A call that has already run is not run again.

beats.heading: Archboard brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. Archboard passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news that names the checkout of the workhorse. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While a recording holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. Pane news goes to the voice model alone, and only for what the user changed by hand.

beats.heading: An approval is answered once
beats.body: A final spoken reply arms a gate on one approval. Whether it is then answered out loud or in the pane, it settles exactly once, and an unproven answer falls back to the narrowest outcome.

beats.heading: Each tab hears only its own threads
beats.body: A tool call or notification goes to the tab session that owns its thread. So a coordinator's tool call runs against the workhorse its own tab has in the checkout the call names, and a workhorse's news reaches only its own tab's coordinator. A tool call from a thread that no tab session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a separate thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It works in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so it names a checkout with -C on every command. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, which goes on working while it talks. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked
beats.body: What the coordinator may ask for is a reviewed template that the host's tool namespace names fill, pinned by the digest of the bytes Codex is given. Every call is matched to its role by that name and digest and validated before it runs. A call that has already run is not run again.

beats.heading: The server brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. The server passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news that names the checkout of the workhorse. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While a recording holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. Pane news goes to the voice model alone, and only for what the user changed by hand.

beats.heading: An approval is answered once
beats.body: A final spoken reply arms a gate on one approval. Whether it is then answered out loud or in the pane, it settles exactly once, and an unproven answer falls back to the narrowest outcome.

beats.heading: Each tab hears only its own threads
beats.body: A tool call or notification goes to the tab session that owns its thread. So a coordinator's tool call runs against the workhorse its own tab has in the checkout the call names, and a workhorse's news reaches only its own tab's coordinator. A tool call from a thread that no tab session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.

nodes.responsibility: Gives the coordinator one piece of news as one turn/start, joining its running turn or starting one, and nothing while the live voice session is unattended
nodes.description: The prompt says what happened and what to do with it: say it under [FINAL] if the user is waiting on it, keep it to a [COMMENTARY] line otherwise, and start no new work because of it.

nodes.name: Tab sessions
nodes.responsibility: Sends each tool call and notification to the tab session whose thread it names: that session's coordinator tools and callbacks, and its workhorses
nodes.description: Each tab session has its own coordinator, coordinator tools, callbacks, realtime voice and spoken approval, and one workhorse for each checkout, so two tabs can talk at the same time. A notification for a thread that no tab session owns yet goes to every session. A tool call from such a thread is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody. It stops the workhorses of its tab session for the coordinator's stop tool, and it notes the conversation shown when each coordinator turn starts.

nodes.name: Thread unload
nodes.responsibility: Unsubscribes a thread once no turn and no voice session runs on it, so Codex unloads it
nodes.description: It reads the thread's status first, then follows the child's notifications until the thread is idle and its voice session has closed. The thread keeps its history on disk either way. The module is reached through createCodexThreadUnload from its root; the returned unload method implements this responsibility.

nodes.name: Workhorse links
nodes.responsibility: Finds the workhorse a callback is about: the ready link whose thread the event names

nodes.name: Coordinator turn homes
nodes.responsibility: Remembers, for each coordinator turn, the conversation shown when it started and the checkouts it gave work to, so the page shows the turn in the right conversation
nodes.description: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown.

nodes.name: Thread and voice
nodes.responsibility: Starts the tab's coordinator thread with its authored instructions, runs the realtime voice leg on it, and unloads a thread that a fresh one replaced

nodes.name: Tools and work

nodes.name: Coordinator news

nodes.name: Host role instructions

nodes.name: Archboard role policy

nodes.name: Host toolset
nodes.responsibility: The built-in tool namespaces as the host names them: each role's reviewed template filled with the host's name, digested over the bytes Codex gets, and the role a call came through
nodes.description: createVoiceToolset fills the workhorse and voice templates of the tool contract and the coordinator's tell_coordinator namespace with the host's names, and the product name for the callback's description. toolRoleOf answers which role a call came through by its namespace and manifest digest, so nothing past the Codex boundary compares a literal name. Archboard names them archboard_workhorse, archboard_voice and archboard_coordinator; a host that names none gets voice_workhorse, voice_channel and voice_coordinator.

nodes.name: Board catalogue
nodes.responsibility: Archboard's context for the coordinator: the catalogue of the boards and variants in the vault of the pane the session presents through, read whole
nodes.description: Realtime voice reads it as the brief of each voice start, and keeps it on the coordinator's thread while voice is live: when the presenting vault or its boards change, the whole catalogue is read again and replaces the one before.

nodes.name: Archboard announcements
nodes.responsibility: Archboard's board changes, focus and selection, worded for the coordinator and the voice and announced through the voice agent
nodes.description: The voice hears the news of a board on screen, as speech when it stops the narration, and nothing of a board no pane shows. The coordinator hears only what an agent outside the session did: a board it wrote, or a pane it moved with browser show. A focus or selection the user made carries a topic, so a later one replaces it while it waits.

nodes.name: Context announcements

nodes.description: With no voice session the receipt says voice_inactive and nothing is queued. Each audience the change names is its own callback, so the coordinator and the voice are told independently, in no fixed order.

walkthroughs.name: Why voice is its own thread

beats.heading: Two threads, two jobs
beats.body: Each tab session has its own coordinator, a separate thread with its own model and settings, started with the tab's first message or Talk. It works in a directory of its own that holds no vault, so it names a checkout with -C on every command. It is the voice model's subconscious: it reads the boards, follows the workhorses and decides what the voice model says. It answers, investigates a little, and hands anything sustained to the workhorse of the checkout it names, which goes on working while it talks. Two tabs can talk at the same time, each to its own coordinator.

beats.heading: The tools are frozen, and checked
beats.body: What the coordinator may ask for is a reviewed template that the host's tool namespace names fill, pinned by the digest of the bytes Codex is given. Every call is matched to its role by that name and digest and validated before it runs. A call that has already run is not run again.

beats.heading: The server brokers, it does not speak
beats.body: The tab makes the peer connection and carries the audio. The server passes the offer to the child and the answer back, and never holds a voice endpoint of its own.

beats.heading: The workhorse's news arrives at once
beats.body: A workhorse turn that ends or begins waiting on the user, whoever started it, and anything the workhorse says through tell_coordinator become one sentence of workhorse news that names the checkout of the workhorse. It goes out as one turn/start, which Codex adds to the coordinator's running turn or starts a turn with, so nothing waits for the coordinator to be idle and nothing enters its history without a turn that acts on it. What it answers under [FINAL] is spoken; a [COMMENTARY] line stays quiet.

beats.heading: Nobody is told without a listener
beats.body: With no voice session the coordinator never runs, so no news is sent and tell_coordinator answers that nobody is listening. While an unattended session holds the voice the outcome report sends nothing, because nobody listens live: in Archboard that is a recording, and whatever the coordinator answered would be spoken into the video. A context change reaches the coordinator and the voice only as the host words it: Archboard tells the voice what changed on a board on screen, and the coordinator only what an agent outside the session did.

beats.heading: An approval is answered once
beats.body: A final spoken reply arms a gate on one approval. Whether it is then answered out loud or in the pane, it settles exactly once, and an unproven answer falls back to the narrowest outcome.

beats.heading: Each tab hears only its own threads
beats.body: A tool call or notification goes to the tab session that owns its thread. So a coordinator's tool call runs against the workhorse its own tab has in the checkout the call names, and a workhorse's news reaches only its own tab's coordinator. A tool call from a thread that no tab session owns is refused, so a running turn never waits on nobody.
